full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim J: By filing an application under section 10 (1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 the accused petitioner has challenged the legality and propriety of the order dated 7-2-2017 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No. 3, Dhaka in Special Case No. 4 of 2012 arising out of ACC GR No. 97 of 2011 corresponding to Cantonment Police Station Case No. 13 dated 22-9-2011 allowing the application for tender of pardon filed by two co-accused namely M Shahjad Ali and Tahmina Ali and thereby treated them as approver. 

 3. In the midst of the trial as per the direction made by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.51837 of 2014 PW-6 M Shahjad Ali and PW 7 Tahmina Ali have been made accused in this case. 

 8. The learned Advocates for the accused petitioner submit that the learned Special Judge beyond the scope of law has passed the impugned order accepting the tender of pardon of said two accused as they have been transposed as accused by the order of High Court Division. They further submit in passing the impugned order the learned Special Judge in fact has frustrated the orders passed in Civil Petition of leave to Appeal No. 60 by the Appellate Division and Miscellaneous Case No.51837 of 2014 by the High Division. 

 11. Having regard to the fact that the accused Shahjad Ali and Tahmina Ali, who were examined PW 6 and PW 7 respectively, have been transposed as accused in the instant case pursuant to the order of the High Court Division passed in Miscellaneous Case No.51837 of 2014. 

 "Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in the case of any offence specified in the Schedule, at any stage of investigation, enquiry, and trial the Special Judge, with a view to obtaining the evidence of any person supposed to have been directly or indirectly concerned in or privy to the offence, may for reasons to be recorded in writing tender pardon to such person on condition of his making a full and true disclosure of the whole of the circumstances within his knowledge relative to the offence and to every other person concerned, whether as principal or abettor, in the commission thereof and any pardon so tendered shall, for the purposes of sections 339 and 339A of the said Code, be deemed to have been tendered under section 337, or, as the case may be, under section 338 of that Code. 

 Provided that in every case where a person has accepted a pardon deemed to have been tendered under section 337 the Magistrate shall, without making any further enquiry, send the case for trial to the Court of the Special Judge having Jurisdiction over such case." 

 17. The High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 51837 of 2015, reported in 68 DLR 67, has observed to the effect that: 

 "The offence of money laundering is thus clearly disclosed in the ejahar and charge sheet against the said M Shahjad Ali and Tahmina Aii Alongside, it also discloses the offence of criminal misconduct under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Despite having clear involvement in the alleged occurrence, their exclusion from the prosecution cannot be validated. It cannot be a pleasure of ACC to prosecute a particular person keeping aside his accomplices. Without making them accused and tendering pardon the status of M Shahjad Ali and Tahmina Ali cannot be simple witnesses." 

 "The Special Judge, Court No. 3, Dhaka is, therefore, directed to treat M Shahjad Ali, son of late Eskandar Ali, and Tahmina Ali, wife of M Shahjad Ali, both of House No.14, Road No.104, Gulshan-2, Dhaka as accused in this case and to take cognizance against them under the relevant provisions of law and proceed in accordance with law. Since charge-sheet has been submitted with a sanction accorded from the Commission, no further sanction would be required in taking such cognizance against them. Their depositions will be deemed to have not been recorded, and it will not be treated as a part of record." 

 20. High Court Division directed the Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka to treat M. Shahjad Ali and Tahmina Ali as accused in this case and to take cognizance against them under the relevant provisions of law and proceed in accordance with law.
